item.title: Taxpayer-funded housing for illegal immigrants in GOP's crosshairs: 'It's got to stop'
item.description: Sen. Bill Hagerty's bill would require citizenship verification for public housing and block sanctuary cities from community development block grants.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: Sen. Bill Hagerty, R-Tenn., is introducing new legislation that works to restrict illegal aliens from reaping federal housing benefits, blocking loopholes and cutting off access for sanctuary cities to receive federal community development grants.

"[Illegal immigrants] have been allowed to participate in federally subsidized housing programs," Hagerty told Fox News Digital. "They're using American taxpayer dollars to jump to the front of the line while putting Americans at the back of the lines. It's got to stop."

The "End Housing Welfare for Illegal Aliens Act" is part of a larger effort by both the Trump administration and GOP members of Congress to halt illegal immigrants and sanctuary cities' ability to thrive, which they claim, often comes at the expense of benefits for the American people.

HOUSE REPUBLICANS MOVE TO MAKE TRUMP'S BORDER POLICIES PERMANENT

"The Trump administration has taken a look at this," Hagerty said. "The preliminary estimates are 24,000 of these illegals are utilizing HUD programs." He continued, "Again, crowding out Americans that would be deserving of these programs, and again, putting illegals into these positions."

The bill Hagerty is putting forward codifies the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) efforts to close loopholes that allow for illegal immigrants to receive federal benefits on taxpayer-funded housing if they are roommates with eligible individuals.

"HUD housing assistance is intended for U.S. citizens and certain eligible noncitizens, yet HUD resources serve only a quarter of eligible households in need," HUD said in a statement. "Meanwhile, a recent HUD and DHS audit of all assisted households identified nearly 200,000 tenants with incomplete or unknown eligibility verification. Furthermore, HUD estimates approximately 24,000 illegal aliens, ineligibles, and fraudsters in 20,000 "mixed status households" benefit from HUD assistance."

Hagerty’s bill, if passed, would enforce this proposed rule by HUD Secretary Scott Turner under all administrations.

"This current administration is going to do everything it can, I'm certain, to stop this type of fraudulent behavior," Hagerty said. "But what I want to do is preclude this from happening if there were ever to be another Democrat administration."

GOP SENATORS RALLY AROUND NEW DHS PROPOSAL TARGETING SANCTUARY CITIES: 'SHOULD PAY A PRICE'

Hagerty also said that the legislation would eliminate Biden-era incentives for sanctuary cities by denying these cities access to Community Development Block Grants (CBDG) — federal funding that supports affordable housing, infrastructure and local services.

He also argued that under the Biden Administration, the adoption of sanctuary city policies was incentivized because those lacking citizenship documentation are still included in population counts when considering congressional representation.

"What the Biden administration did, they were creating incentives for people to come here illegally," Hagerty said. "You think about where they situated sanctuary cities —- in blue states, where they're losing population, where they’re losing voters."

"Why?" Hagerty said. "Because you can count these illegal aliens for the purpose of allocating congressional districts. You can count them for the purpose of locating electoral votes. That is the motive behind the crime."

'AMERICA FIRST' IMMIGRATION OVERHAUL BILL WOULD CODIFY TRUMP'S CAMPAIGN PROMISES ONCE AND FOR ALL

The bill would require public housing authorities to verify citizenship before providing housing assistance. This would change the law so agencies "shall" verify citizenship, meaning they are legally required to do so, instead of saying they only "may" do so.

It would also specifically bar illegal immigrants from being eligible for both Section 202 and Section 811, which provide affordable housing for low-income elderly and people with disabilities.

"Illegal aliens are pushing out and crowding out people that are disabled, American taxpayers that are disabled, elderly that are disabled," Hagerty said.

Hagerty’s efforts to crack down on any negligence in restricting illegal immigrants from federal programs comes amid a broader fight by the Trump administration and Republicans in Congress to crack down on illegal immigration throughout the country.

"The goal is to pass the legislation," Hagerty said. "And I think if you polled Americans, you'd find this is extraordinarily popular."

item.title: Explosive drone forces shutdown at major German airport serving NATO, Ukraine flights
item.description: An explosive-armed drone was found near a Ukrainian plane at Leipzig/Halle Airport, prompting Germany's interior minister to warn of a hybrid attack.
item.content:encoded:
A drone carrying explosives was found near a Ukrainian plane at Germany's Leipzig/Halle Airport late Tuesday, prompting officials to warn the incident represented "a new quality of danger," authorities said Wednesday.

The discovery temporarily shut down both runways at the major European freight hub and forced several flights to divert to other airports, according to The Associated Press.

Another flying object was spotted nearby shortly before midnight and several flights, including one passenger plane, were then diverted to other airports.

JETBLUE FLIGHT REPORTS DRONE STRIKE DURING APPROACH TO NEW YORK AIRPORT: FAA

German police launched a large response and opened an investigation into the two incidents.

Police said an airport worker found the first explosive drone near the airport's south runway with "an unknown explosive device."

An explosives-disposal robot was deployed to examine the device before authorities removed its detonator.

The plane, bearing the blue-and-yellow colors of the Ukrainian flag, displayed the English-language slogan, "Be Brave Like Kherson," a tribute to the southern Ukrainian region, Deutsche Welle reported.

In the second incident, an unidentified flying object collided with a cargo aircraft that had aborted its landing at Leipzig/Halle Airport because of the runway closure.

HELICOPTER REPORTS NEAR MISS WITH RC PLANE NEAR JFK AFTER JETBLUE DRONE STRIKE

The aircraft diverted to Hannover Airport, about 125 miles north-west of Leipzig, where officials found minor damage, according to The Associated Press.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the discovery of the first drone marked a significant escalation.

"Drone sightings, drone threats, including in a hybrid context, are something we know from the past," he said. "That a drone armed with explosives is at an airport is a new threat scenario."

Dobrindt also described the incident as "a hybrid attack scenario."

He said questions about the type of explosives used, the drone's origin and who was responsible remained under investigation.

"All the speculation that is currently going on about the explosives, the construction, the question of the drone, the origin and, of course, who is behind it, is now part of the investigation," Dobrindt said.

"What is happening now also shows that the assessment made months ago — that we are dealing with a high level of danger — was justified," Dobrindt added.

In June, Dobrindt opened Germany's Joint Centre for Countering Hybrid Threats, which brings together federal and state security agencies to address threats including espionage, sabotage and disinformation.

REPORT WARNS RUSSIA USING SHADOW FLEET TO PROBE NATO DRONE DEFENSES

Leipzig/Halle Airport is a major European cargo hub, and Ukrainian Antonov transport aircraft are based there.

NATO said it was aware of the incidents but referred questions to German authorities.

RUSSIA LINKED TO ARSON ATTACKS ON PROPERTIES CONNECTED TO UK PM KEIR STARMER, POLICE SAY

Ukraine's ambassador to Germany, Oleksii Makeiev, suggested Moscow may have been behind the incident, telling Welt TV on Wednesday, "Who else could it be but Russia?" according to reports.

In 2024, an incendiary device ignited at a logistics center at Leipzig/Halle Airport, setting fire to a freight container in an incident Western security officials suspect was part of a Russian intelligence sabotage operation.

item.title: In Nevada speech, Trump chases after toddler on stage before joking he doesn't want him to 'be Biden and fall'
item.description: Trump invited a Las Vegas casino waitress and police officer's family on stage, where their toddler delivered a Trump Account thank-you.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump shared a pair of lighthearted moments with a toddler during a Nevada event Wednesday, first stepping in to stop the young boy from wandering off-stage before joking, "I don't want him to be [former President Joe] Biden and fall off the stage."

The moment unfolded after Trump invited Sandra and Brad, a Las Vegas couple, on stage at the Red Rock Casino Resort and Spa with their two young children as he touted his administration's Trump Accounts and "no tax on tips" initiatives.

As the child's mother, Sandra, began to address the crowd, the toddler appeared ready to make a break for it before Trump quickly reached out to stop him from leaving the stage.

'PAWN STARS' ICON RICK HARRISON SAYS TRUMP TAX POLICIES CHANGE EVERYTHING FOR SMALL BUSINESSES

"I don't want him to be Biden and fall off the stage," Trump quipped, drawing laughter from the audience.

The playful exchange wasn't the family's only memorable moment with the president.

Later, after Sandra told Trump, "He did want to say a little something to you, Mr. President," Trump replied, "Yes, thank you, thank you very much."

The toddler then babbled briefly before his mother softly prompted him, "Thank you for my Trump Account."

DEMOCRATIC MARYLAND GOV WES MOORE PRAISES TRUMP ACCOUNTS AS ‘SMART POLICY’

"Thank you for my Trump Account," the little boy repeated into the microphone, prompting an uproar of applause from the crowd.

"Good job," Trump responded with a smile, clapping for the toddler as the audience continued cheering.

Earlier in the event, Trump introduced the family by explaining that Sandra works as a waitress at a Las Vegas casino, while Brad serves as an officer with the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department.

Trump said the couple had benefited from his administration's tax policies and were investing in Trump Accounts for their two children.

"It's a beautiful family," Trump said as they joined him on stage.

Trump is a father of five and has 11 grandchildren.

item.title: Chiefs coach Andy Reid has a blunt response to everyone freaking out over Travis Kelce's dad bod
item.description: Andy Reid insists Travis Kelce came back in good shape, but practice footage and declining 2025 stats tell a different story for fantasy football owners.
item.content:encoded:
NFL training camp is barely a week old, and the Kansas City Chiefs already find themselves embroiled in a full-blown investigation: Has Travis Kelce succumbed to the dreaded dad bod?

The internet's amateur body-fat analysts went to work last week after pictures of a noticeably thicker Kelce made the rounds.

Chiefs coach Andy Reid wasted little time trying to put out the fat fires Wednesday, telling the media his star tight end is bigger but allegedly in good shape.

FANS STUNNED AT TRAVIS KELCE'S TRAINING CAMP PHYSIQUE AFTER NUPTIALS TO TAYLOR SWIFT

"He came back in good shape," Reid insisted.

"I know everybody's out there saying he's got the dad body and all this stuff, but he looks the same to me that he's always looked, and [he's] playing like crazy." Reid even claimed the veteran is "focused in and ready to go" for every practice snap.

Kelce is officially listed at 250 pounds, but if you apply the eyeball test to the practice footage, that scale might be doing some heavy lifting.

The guy is 36 years old, which is basically 50 in tight end years.

TAYLOR SWIFT MARRIES TRAVIS KELCE

Kelce spent the offseason pounding beers in VIP suites on the Eras Tour, married Taylor Swift in July, and expanded his media empire. He has three Super Bowl rings, infinite money, and a life on easy mode, even if he remembers his six-pack abs all too well.

With all that in mind, you'd be forgiven for wondering why he's still doing this. So why are we dragging this out?

Look at the numbers from last season. In 2025, Kelce posted a modest 76 catches for 851 yards and five touchdowns. For normal mortals, those are decent numbers. For Travis Kelce? That is a clear slide down the hill.

Father Time remains undefeated, and carrying extra offseason weight certainly isn't going to turn back the clock.

HALL OF FAMER CRIS CARTER SAYS UPCOMING NFL SEASON WILL BE TRAVIS KELCE’S ‘LAST DANCE’

Which brings us to the real conspiracy: why is someone in your fantasy league still going to reach for him in the early rounds?

Don't let it be you.

Every August, fantasy owners convince themselves a declining superstar is somehow about to turn back the clock.

Then by Week 4, they're wondering why they burned a premium pick on yesterday's highlights instead of tomorrow's breakout.

Draft upside players, not household names living off past glory. Let someone else chase the nostalgia and pray for one last vintage season.

item.title: Kennedy Center board member knocks Sen Whitehouse for ignoring invites as Dem feuds with Trump-run landmark
item.description: In a letter obtained by Fox News Digital, Kennedy Center Board of Trustees member Brian Ballard called out Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX — A member of the Kennedy Center's board of trustees called out Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., who continues to level "mismanagement" allegations while refusing to accept multiple invitations for in-person meetings.

"Given that Executive Director and Chief Operating Officer Matt Floca's several good-faith invitations for an in-person meeting to address your concerns have gone repeatedly ignored, it appears that written correspondence is your preferred method of communication," Kennedy Center board member Brian Ballard wrote to Whitehouse Wednesday in a letter obtained by Fox News Digital.

"The current leadership of the Kennedy Center has on several occasions provided our board with a transparent and thorough assessment of the scope of work needed to address the Center's decades of deferred maintenance, including well-documented systemic deterioration and public safety hazards. 

"It is my informed opinion that this work cannot be completed safely, or efficiently, around a fully operating public building. I do not believe a board acting responsibly could currently conclude that such an approach is the more prudent course."

KENNEDY CENTER DISPUTES ALLEGATIONS ON CONTRACTOR BIDS DESPITE DEMOCRATIC SENATOR'S CLAIMS

Ballard insisted to Whitehouse that the Kennedy Center's Audit and Finance Committee regularly meets "contrary to your assertion." He also disputed Whitehouse's claim that the "suspension of guided tours that put the consequences of recent mismanagement on full display," telling him that tours were only halted for five days "in part due to administrative management conducting a review of campus-wide tour routes to ensure they provide the best possible experience for visitors and was scheduled to overlap with maintenance work of the sprinkler system across the complex.

"None of this is to wave away the Board's obligations following the Court's decision as I share your view that we owe trustees, Congress, and the public a rigorous, well-documented record of the decisions ahead of us, and I am confident that management will continue to meet that standard," Ballard continued. 

"To echo Matt's repeated invitations, I would welcome the chance to walk through all of this with you directly, in person, rather than by written correspondence — letters which seemingly end up in the hands of the press before they reach the intended recipient to begin with."

‘CONFLICT OF INTEREST’: JUDGE WHO AXED TRUMP NAME FROM DC LANDMARK TIED TO ANTI-TRUMP CONSPIRACY THEORY

Ballard concluded the letter by expressing hope Whitehouse attends the next board meeting, adding, "Despite your rank as ex-officio and supposed concerns, I do believe we share the priority goal of success for our National Cultural Center."

"Political theater has no place at America’s cultural center," Kennedy Center Vice President of Public Relations Roma Daravi said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Our Chairman President Trump’s commitment to revitalization is supported by Center leadership and the Board, who are laser-focused on the responsible stewardship of this beloved institution."

Sen. Whitehouse's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

A source familiar with the matter told Fox News Digital Whitehouse did not attend a board meeting held in March nor attend a scheduled April tour that highlighted the Kennedy Center's maintenance needs. He also avoided multiple invitations by Kennedy Center COO Matt Floca for an in-person discussion.

Whitehouse, who sits on the Environment and Public Works Committee, penned a scathing letter on Monday to Floca, slamming what he called the Kennedy Center's "sorry pattern."

"As you also know, there is widespread suspicion that the decision to 'close for repairs' was a pretext to cover up the gross mismanagement that has crashed bookings, attendance, and revenues," Whitehouse wrote. "There was also an obvious fiduciary question about what the renaming effort would mean for the Center’s business. It was never even considered in the rush to rename."

BILL MAHER SAYS IT'S 'SO STUPID' FOR ANTI-TRUMP ARTISTS TO BAIL ON KENNEDY CENTER PERFORMANCES

The senator later threatened, "If the intention is to drive the Center into financial failure by prevarication and delay in responding to the Court’s order, that would be the very definition of fiduciary failure, and such conduct should be reviewed by counsel, both as to the individual liability Board members may face for negligence and as to the state of the Board’s errors and omissions coverage. We should also hear from counsel about the possible avenues for Court supervision or receivership if no credible revival plan is presented and adopted."

A federal judge in May blocked the Trump administration's plans to shutter the Kennedy Center for a two-year renovation project.

The judge also blocked the renaming of the Kennedy Center to the Trump Kennedy Center, insisting only Congress can change its name.

item.title: Trump has become America's most targeted leader, facing threats every few months
item.description: President Donald Trump has survived three assassination attempts and nearly 20 known threats total, making him the most targeted U.S. president on public record.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump has become the most targeted U.S. leader on record among both sitting and former presidents, facing threat-related incidents roughly every two to three months in recent years.

Trump has survived three major assassination attempts and nearly a dozen other threat-related incidents over the past two years alone. Overall, he has faced nearly 20 known threats since first taking office in 2017.

By comparison, every other U.S. president targeted in an assassination attempt faced just one, except President Gerald R. Ford, who survived two. Those presidents include Andrew Jackson, Abraham Lincoln, James A. Garfield, William McKinley, Theodore Roosevelt, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Harry Truman, John F. Kennedy, Gerald R. Ford, Ronald Reagan, Bill Clinton, George W. Bush and Barack Obama. 

Four of those presidents — Lincoln, Garfield, McKinley and Kennedy — were killed.

FROM TRAINED ASSASSINS TO RALLY STAGE RUSHERS, HERE'S EVERY KNOWN ATTEMPT ON TRUMP'S LIFE SINCE 2016

Seven known threat-related incidents occurred during Trump's first presidency, while four occurred during his 2024 campaign, including two assassination attempts. His second presidency has already seen eight additional incidents, including a third assassination attempt.

July 2024: The first assassination attempt on Trump came during a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, when a gunman opened fire from a nearby rooftop, killing one spectator and critically wounding two others. The shooter, 20-year-old Thomas Matthew Crooks, struck Trump in the upper right ear before being killed by a Secret Service sniper.

September 2024: Two months later, Secret Service agents spotted a gunman hiding in bushes with a rifle near Trump's Florida golf course while the then-presidential candidate was golfing. The suspect, Ryan Wesley Routh, was arrested and later sentenced to life in prison.

TWO MEN SHOT AT TRUMP'S BUTLER RALLY SUE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OVER SECRET SERVICE 'PREVENTABLE FAILURES'

April 2026: A major security breach occurred during the White House Correspondents' Dinner while Trump was in attendance. The suspect, Cole Allen, allegedly charged a security checkpoint armed with multiple weapons, shot an officer and was later taken into custody.

Trump's first three security incidents unfolded during his 2016 campaign before he ever took office.

March 2016: An attendee at a Trump campaign rally in Dayton, Ohio, attempted to rush the stage before being arrested. The suspect, Thomas DiMassimo, 22, told police he intended to grab the microphone and shout that Trump was a racist but reportedly did not intend to harm him. He was later sentenced to one year of probation.

June 2016: Three months later, a British national attending a Trump campaign rally in Las Vegas attempted to grab a police officer's handgun from her holster, according to a federal criminal complaint. The suspect, Michael Steven Sandford, initially told an officer he wanted Trump's autograph before trying to seize the weapon and later admitting he intended to kill Trump. He was sentenced to 12 months and one day in prison.

November 2016: Secret Service agents rushed Trump off the stage during a campaign rally in Reno, Nevada, after an attendee shouted "gun." Authorities found no weapon but briefly detained Austyn Crites, 33, who said he had brought a sign that said "Republicans Against Trump." Trump returned to the stage minutes later to finish his remarks.

September 2017: A man stole a forklift and drove it toward Trump's presidential motorcade in an apparent attempt to overturn the presidential limousine in North Dakota. The suspect, Gregory Lee Leingang, later pleaded guilty to federal charges and was sentenced in 2019 to time served and one year of supervised release.

October 2018: A Navy veteran in Utah was charged after ricin-laced letters addressed to Trump and other officials were intercepted before delivery. William Clyde Allen III was charged with five federal counts but was later found incompetent to assist in his defense.

August 2020: Trump was abruptly escorted out of a briefing room during a televised news conference after a Secret Service officer shot a man who threatened to kill people near the White House. The suspect, Myron Basil Berryman, 51, of Forestville, Maryland, was found unarmed and arrested on a charge of assaulting a law enforcement officer, according to the Metropolitan Police Department.

September 2020: A suspect mailed a ricin-laced letter to Trump that was intercepted before reaching the White House. The sender, Pascale Cecile Veronique Ferrier, a dual citizen of Canada and France, admitted to manufacturing ricin at her home in Canada and was later sentenced to 262 months in prison, equivalent to more than 21 years, followed by lifetime supervised release.

Trump then faced two assassination attempts and two additional threat-related incidents during his 2024 presidential campaign.

July 2024: One day prior to the Butler assassination attempt, federal authorities arrested a Pakistani national accused of orchestrating a murder-for-hire plot targeting Trump and other U.S. officials on behalf of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The suspect, Asif Merchant, was later convicted in federal court in March 2026.

November 2024: After the second assassination attempt on Trump in September 2024, the Justice Department disclosed another alleged Iranian murder-for-hire plot targeting Trump. The suspect, Farhad Shakeri, was accused of being an Iranian government asset who had been tasked with planning the assassination of Trump. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said in March 2026 that Shakeri had been killed in a U.S. military operation.

Just 1½ years into his second presidency, Trump has faced seven additional threat-related incidents and one assassination attempt.

May 2025: A Florida man was arraigned in federal court after allegedly writing a letter to an official at the Charlotte Correctional Institution claiming he had "orchestrated the most daring Presidential assassination that this country has ever seen" and that "Donald J. Trump must perish." The suspect, Christopher Davies, later admitted he wanted to kill Trump and was sentenced to 27 months in federal prison.

July 2025: Authorities arrested a Texas man after he allegedly threatened Trump on social media ahead of the president's visit to the state following the July 4 flooding along the Guadalupe River. The suspect, Robert Herrera, was later sentenced to two years in prison.

August 2025: Authorities arrested a Georgia man after he allegedly posted a comment on a TikTok livestream threatening to shoot Trump. The suspect, 29-year-old Jauan Rashun Porter, wrote, "So there's only one way to make America great and that is putting a bullet in between Trump's eyes." He was later sentenced to more than three years in federal prison.

FBI DISRUPTS ALLEGED EXPLOSIVE-DRONE PLOT TARGETING WHITE HOUSE UFC EVENT, OFFICIALS SAY

February 2026: An armed man drove into the secure perimeter of Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach as another vehicle was exiting the property. The suspect, 21-year-old Austin Tucker Martin, was fatally shot by authorities.

April 2026: Officials unsealed a federal criminal complaint against a Kentucky man accused of posting a series of politically violent threats on Instagram between January and late March 2026. 

The suspect, 23-year-old Kadrioan Serainity Santiago, allegedly threatened to cut Trump with a razor blade and feed his skin to stray dogs. He also threatened to kill the next member of law enforcement who interacted with him, encouraged violence against ICE agents and posted comments saying, "I’m filled with political violence."

June 2026: Law enforcement officials uncovered an alleged terrorism conspiracy targeting Trump's UFC event at the White House just four days before the mixed martial arts event was scheduled to take place. Eight men were indicted in an alleged plot to fly explosive-laden drones into the event and open fire on attendees as they fled, according to authorities.

August 2026: Authorities arrested a suspect who was allegedly photographing and recording security preparations ahead of a scheduled fundraising dinner at the Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes, California. The suspect, Jeanine John Taele, 38, was found carrying a 16-round magazine loaded with ammunition, while investigators recovered an additional pistol and a fake "security protection agent" badge from his truck.

item.title: Diddy's federal prison release delayed weeks after reported solitary confinement stint
item.description: Sean Diddy Combs' federal prison release date was pushed back to Feb. 20, 2028, after he was reportedly sent to solitary confinement after a prison fight.
item.content:encoded:
Sean "Diddy" Combs' federal prison release date has changed once again.

Diddy, 56, is now expected to leave prison Feb. 20, 2028, nearly one month after his previously scheduled release date, according to the Federal Bureau of Prisons. 

Diddy's release date has changed multiple times since he began serving his sentence.  

According to multiple reports, the disgraced rap mogul was reportedly sent to solitary confinement last month after a prison fight with another inmate.

DIDDY SENT TO SOLITARY CONFINEMENT AFTER PRISON FIGHT WITH ANOTHER INMATE: MULTIPLE REPORTS

The incident began after a fellow inmate "made a remark to Combs, which instigated the event" at FCI Fort Dix, ABC News reported at the time.

Diddy was then reportedly sent to solitary confinement, the outlet noted. It's unclear if his release date was delayed due to the reported fight.

CASSIE VENTURA FLED THE UNITED STATES AFTER TESTIFYING AGAINST DIDDY IN SEX CRIMES TRIAL: DOCS

"For privacy, safety and security reasons, we do not release information regarding the conditions of confinement for any inmate, including housing assignments, nor do we discuss whether a particular inmate is the subject of allegations, investigations or sanctions," a representative for the Federal Bureau of Prisons told Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Diddy's representatives declined Fox News Digital's request for comment.

In September 2024, the "Last Night" singer was arrested on federal sex trafficking charges after months of sexual misconduct allegations, lawsuits, investigations and the release of surveillance video that appeared to show the rapper severely beating then-girlfriend Cassie in the hallway of a Los Angeles hotel. 

He was sentenced to more than four years behind bars in October after being convicted in July on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Diddy initially faced a maximum of life in prison if convicted on charges that included racketeering conspiracy, sex trafficking by force, coercion and transportation to engage in prostitution.

A jury convicted Diddy on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution July 2, 2025. The "I'll Be Missing You" rapper was acquitted of the most serious charges of racketeering and sex trafficking.

In addition to the 50-month sentence, Diddy was ordered to serve five years of supervised release and pay a $500,000 fine. The prosecution recommended 135 months (just over 11 years) for his sentencing.

item.title: Social media users are having a hard time processing LaMelo Ball's Charlotte penthouse
item.description: A viral video from movers packing up LaMelo Ball's Charlotte penthouse reveals alien mannequins, neon lights and an interior unlike anything else.
item.content:encoded:
The Charlotte Hornets traded LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves this offseason after six seasons with the team, which means that at least a portion of his offseason activities has involved moving.

But when it comes to boxing up his place, Ball's pad is not like anything most of us are used to, and not just because it's a penthouse.

A mover working at the apartment posted a video on social media that quickly went viral because... well, you don't see a lot of apartments with alien mannequins standing on countertops that look like a NASA photo of a distant galaxy.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

If you've ever wondered what happens when you give a 24-year-old an almost limitless amount of money, we finally have an answer.

It turns out that, at least in the case of Ball, he pretty much turned his place into what looks like every retro arcade bar I've ever been to, sans the actual arcade cabinets.

Just aliens and neon every which way you look.

I don't know about you, but I'd find it hard to relax in my penthouse with an alien basketball player staring at me from atop my kitchen counter and a neon sign of some cartoon character flickering from down the hall.

But maybe that's just me.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

This video quickly went viral for obvious reasons, and social media users had some thoughts and observations of their own.

Hey, to each their own.

I will say, however, that "Alien Clown Core" might be the best description of whatever that was. It was like LaMelo's interior decorator (I'm going to assume he didn't use one, but let's pretend for a moment) asked him for some photo inspirations and just handed her a Blu-Ray copy of "Killer Klowns from Outer Space."

Well, we'll have to wait and see if Ball brings Alien Clown Core to the Twin Cities or if he tones things down a little bit.

item.title: Martha Stewart gets candid about plastic surgery, dating as she turns 85
item.description: Martha Stewart shared a hot tub photo from her Maine estate on her 85th birthday and revealed to People magazine she has never had plastic surgery.
item.content:encoded:
Martha Stewart isn't planning to go under the knife or settle down with an older partner.

The lifestyle icon is embracing turning 85 on her own terms, opening up about plastic surgery, dating and aging in a new interview as she celebrated the milestone birthday.

Stewart doubled down on her long-held approach to aging naturally, revealing she has never undergone plastic surgery despite decades in the public eye.

JANE SEYMOUR, 75, SHARES HOW SHE APPROACHES AGING WITH VITALITY: 'BEST I CAN BE'

"I have not had any plastic surgery at all. I don't think I need it," Stewart told People magazine.

Instead, Stewart said she relies on consistent skin care, facial treatments and healthy habits to maintain her appearance.

"I use a little bit of fillers," she explained. "I go maybe once every four months for touch-ups.

"I'm more a maintenance kind of person. I'm not getting boobs done and hips and butts and stuff like that."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Stewart also opened up about her outlook on relationships later in life, saying companionship has become less important as she's gotten older.

"Now, it's less important," she said when asked whether she still envies friends with happy marriages. "The older you get, the less you really need a mate, I think.

"I wouldn't want to be beleaguered with an older, ill person."

Stewart also marked her 85th birthday by sharing a photo of herself relaxing in a bubbling hot tub during a stay in Maine.

She appeared to be unwinding at her sprawling Maine estate, where she soaked in the steaming water while wearing a black swimsuit. Evergreen trees surrounded the tranquil setting, with a sprawling pool stretching out behind the hot tub.

'KNOTS LANDING' STAR DONNA MILLS SAYS SHE WON'T 'BE QUIET' AFTER CRITIC TARGETED HER MAKEUP AT AGE 85

"I am going to use this amazing hot tub every single day I am in maine," Stewart wrote alongside the photo. "Invigorating restorative Therapeutic relaxing."

Fans quickly flooded the comments with compliments, with one writing, "Damn serving face too," while another added, "Martha you are everything truly."

The birthday milestone comes as Stewart continues embracing getting older on her own terms.

"I don't think about age," she told People. "Eighty-five is just a number; that's all I consider it. I don't want to have a party. It's not a big deal.

"My goal is to keep learning about everything."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Stewart credited much of her youthful appearance to the lifestyle she has maintained for decades.

"I have good genes. My mom looked great at 95," she said. "We eat well. We don't drink very much. We don't smoke. We eat healthy food. We exercise daily. I horseback-ride."

Stewart's disciplined routine extends well beyond her diet. She told People she still wakes at 3 a.m. every morning to complete her daily puzzles before starting her day.

Turning 85 hasn't slowed Stewart down.

The lifestyle entrepreneur recently recreated her 1995 People cover at her 156-acre Bedford, New York, farm, where she reflected on the career that made her the country's best-known homemaking authority.

ROSIE O'DONNELL WALKED AWAY AT THE HEIGHT OF HER SUCCESS AFTER REACHING ONE JAW-DROPPING FINANCIAL MILESTONE

"I still am a perfectionist. I still like to do many things at the same time. I like to do all the same things I've pretty much always done," Stewart said. "I'd like to have a little bit more free time. I don't have any free time at all, but I'm working on that."

Raised in Nutley, New Jersey, Stewart began modeling before launching a catering business and publishing her first cookbook, "Entertaining," helping build an empire that expanded into magazines, television, retail partnerships and home products. She became the first self-made female billionaire in the United States in 1999.

She has since authored more than 100 cookbooks, opened restaurants, become the oldest Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover model at age 81 and continues adding new ventures to her résumé, including her home intelligence app Hint, a skin care line and multiple brand partnerships.

Asked whether she already has everything she wants, Stewart pointed to her newest venture.

"No, I don't. I didn't have an app for my home, and so I'm making one," she said.

item.title: American Airlines flight attendant's alleged killers tied to gang accused of preying on tourists: officials
item.description: Two suspects captured in Peru months after allegedly drugging and killing American Airlines flight attendant Eric Fernando Gutierrez Molina in Medellín.
item.content:encoded:
Two men accused of drugging and killing an American Airlines flight attendant during a layover in Colombia have been arrested months after the slaying, authorities said, with the suspects allegedly tied to a gang known to prey on tourists.

Andrés Felipe Peña Corrales, 23, and William Olave Gamboa, 31, were captured in Peru in connection with the March killing of Eric Fernando Gutierrez Molina, 32, a Dallas-based flight attendant whose disappearance in Medellín sparked an international search.

Peña Corrales has since been transferred to Colombia to face charges, while Olave Gamboa remains in Peruvian custody awaiting extradition proceedings. Both men face charges including aggravated homicide and aggravated robbery in Colombia, according to authorities.

AMERICANS WARNED POPULAR TRAVEL ROUTES THIS SUMMER COULD CARRY CRIME AND KIDNAPPING RISKS

A third suspect, María del Carmen González, 24, was arrested separately in Montería, Colombia. Investigators allege she was not directly involved in Gutierrez Molina’s killing but participated in withdrawing and moving money stolen from foreign victims as part of the group’s operation.

Colombian police identified all three suspects as alleged members of Los Goteros, a criminal organization accused of targeting foreign tourists by contacting them through dating apps, gaining their trust, drugging them and stealing money, jewelry and other valuables.

According to reporting by El Colombiano, investigators believe Gutierrez Molina was contacted through a dating app before meeting several people at a nightclub in Medellín’s El Poblado neighborhood.

The group later went to a hotel, where Gutierrez Molina and his coworker were allegedly drugged before their belongings were stolen and their financial accounts were accessed, the outlet reported.

The outlet also reported that scopolamine, sometimes called "Devil’s Breath" or "Dragon’s Breath," may have been used to incapacitate the victims, though authorities have not publicly confirmed toxicology findings in the case.

Gutierrez Molina was reportedly strangled, while his coworker survived.

DATING-APP CHARMER ACCUSED OF MURDER AFTER HISTORY OF DOMESTIC ARRESTS INVOLVING WOMEN HE MET ONLINE

Investigators allege the group accessed Gutierrez Molina’s bank accounts, stole other valuables and abandoned his body near Jericó, southwest of Medellín, where it was found five days later.

The arrests capped a months-long international investigation involving U.S. Homeland Security Investigations, Colombian prosecutors and Peruvian authorities.

"This successful outcome reflects the strong commitment of the United States, Colombia and Peru to work together to investigate and bring to justice a group of criminals in Colombia dedicated to the robbery and theft of U.S. citizens and ensure the safety of international travelers in the region," the U.S. Embassy in Colombia said in a joint statement.

The embassy also recognized the Mayor’s Office of Medellín, Colombia’s National Police and Peru’s National Police for their roles in the investigation.

EXCLUSIVE: ALLEGED $32M COVID-19 FRAUD FUGITIVE CAPTURED IN JAMAICA AND RETURNED TO US, FBI SAYS

Gutierrez Molina disappeared in March while on an overnight layover in Medellín before he was scheduled to continue to Miami.

Friends told local media at the time that he shared his location from an Airbnb near José María Córdova International Airport before communication suddenly stopped, prompting coworkers and family members to report him missing.

Days later, Medellín Mayor Federico Gutiérrez announced that authorities had recovered a body near Jericó. The remains were later identified as Gutierrez Molina.

"We are heartbroken by the tragic passing of our colleague," American Airlines said in a statement previously provided to Fox News Digital.

"Our thoughts and support are with his family, loved ones and colleagues during this difficult time, and we are doing all we can to assist Colombian law enforcement in its investigation."

Authorities said investigators are working to determine whether additional foreign tourists were victimized by Los Goteros using the same alleged scheme.

Fox News Digital's Alex Koch and Alex Nitzberg contributed to this report.

item.title: Clay Travis tells Dan Dakich about his $10 million offer to the Las Vegas Aces and how Elon Musk could help

CLAY TRAVIS UPS OFFER TO $10 MILLION FOR WNBA CHAMPION LAS VEGAS ACES TO PLAY HIGH SCHOOL BOYS BASKETBALL TEAM

item.title: Pete Buttigieg distances himself from Biden amid 2028 talk, suggests 'Build Back Better' doesn't work
item.description: Pete Buttigieg distanced himself from former President Joe Biden's "Build Back Better" message and rejected a "return to normal" strategy amid 2028 rumors.
item.content:encoded:
Former Transportation Secretary and potential 2028 presidential candidate Pete Buttigieg appeared to distance himself from former President Joe Biden and rejected the idea of a "return to normal" during a Politico interview Tuesday.

"I'm trying to purge my vocabulary of anything with the prefix 're-' in it, anything with the word back in it," Buttigieg told columnist Jonathan Martin. "I don't think now is the time to be talking about 'Build Back Better.' Build better, yes. I don't even want to talk about back."

Martin pointed out that "Build Back Better" was Biden's 2020 presidential campaign slogan and asked if that meant he believed the party has changed in the last six years.

JAMES CARVILLE ARGUES ONE KEY MISTAKE FROM BIDEN HAS LEFT DEMOCRATS IN DISARRAY

"Yeah, I mean, I think, you know, if that could have worked, it would have worked," Buttigieg said.

Overall, Buttigieg rejected the idea of pushing a "return to normal" message that was the staple of Biden's original campaign.

"But to me, the most important thing is — are we demonstrating a readiness to be focused on building what’s next or are we basically preaching some version of 'return to normal'? 'Return to normal,' in my view, won’t work."

"One way to say I’m not a 'return to normal' is to present the idea that looks furthest left, because that makes you, in a certain way, seem bold. I don’t think it’s the only way to be bold. And so, I think it is really important to not let it lapse into a 'left versus center' thing, when the most important question to me is, are we going to try to sell some version of a previous status quo?" Buttigieg said.

BUTTIGIEG REVEALS HOW HE'D ADVISE DEMOCRATS ON KEY ISSUES IF HE COULD TIME TRAVEL BACK TO 2020

The former Biden official also "couldn't say" the former president was a mentor to him, though he referred to him as a "good man" and a "good boss."

"I wasn't close enough to him to say that," Buttigieg said. "But I would say that he, again, after I competed against him, and he beat me and everybody else in that primary, he gave me a tremendous opportunity to do a lot of work that I cared about, that was meaningful, that I'm proud of ... I learned a lot from him, but I wouldn't say I was close enough to him that I claim that."

Fox News Digital reached out to Biden's office for comment but did not immediately receive a response. 

Buttigieg's comments came after a University of New Hampshire Granite State Poll published last month showed him neck-and-neck with Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., in a potential 2028 match-up, though he has yet to fully commit to another presidential run.

KAMALA HARRIS LEAVES BIDEN OFF LIST OF TOP THREE 'MOST EFFECTIVE' PRESIDENTS

In light of this, Buttigieg has doubled down on far-left proposals such as eliminating the Electoral College or expanding the Supreme Court while downplaying concerns over the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and its candidates.

"I think one of the reasons why you see people who run on a promise of shaking it up, whether it's a DSA candidate on the left or whether it’s someone like Donald Trump, is because people can tell that the system we have is not just showing its age — it's letting us down," Buttigieg said on "America Reports."

The comment drew criticism from Fox News political analyst Reince Priebus, who served as RNC chairman and White House chief of staff to President Donald Trump in his first term, warning that Democrats like Buttigieg are aligning with people on "the wrong side of normal."

"The opponent — the Democrats from where Pete Buttigieg is at — is aligning itself with people that are far outside the mainstream. They're on the wrong side of normal, and he didn't really address that when he was pressed," Priebus said on "America Reports." "And that's the big question for him."

item.title: Dems in the hot seat for skipping crucial hearing on radical group hiding in US: 'Embarrassment'
item.description: Every Democratic Party member of a Senate Judiciary subcommittee boycotted a hearing on the Muslim Brotherhood's alleged U.S. network, describing the hearing as "a political creepshow."
item.content:encoded:
Democratic lawmakers were missing during Wednesday's Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing, skipping a hearing on the Muslim Brotherhood’s alleged network inside the United States and drawing a blistering rebuke from Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas.

"You may notice that there are empty chairs on the Democrat side of the dais," Cruz said as he opened the hearing by pointing out every Democratic member of the subcommittee refused to attend. "The American people should ask themselves why not a single member of the minority decided that a hearing on terrorism was worth their time? It is an embarrassment."

Cruz tied the Democrats’ boycott to Abdul El-Sayed’s primary victory, arguing the timing helped explain why no Democratic members attended. Cruz accused the party of embracing a candidate who had campaigned alongside left-wing streamer Hasan Piker. 

Cruz cited Piker’s past statement that "America deserved 9/11" and asked the witnesses what El-Sayed’s rise said about the direction of the Democratic Party.

HASAN PIKER UNLOADS ON 'ISLAMOPHOBIC PIECES OF S---' DEMOCRATS AS EL-SAYED FACES PARTY UNITY TEST

"Abdul El-Sayed, the son-in-law of a leading member of several Brotherhood groups, won Michigan’s Democrat primary for U.S. Senate. Perfect timing for this hearing. Probably explains why no Democrats are here, and none intend to attend," Cruz said. 

"Because their campaign is now openly embracing terrorist organizations waging war on America."

The five Democratic members of the subcommittee — senators Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut, Mazie Hirono of Hawaii, Alex Padilla of California and Peter Welch of Vermont — announced beforehand that they would not attend. In a joint statement, the senators accused Cruz of staging a "political creepshow" that scapegoated Muslim Americans.

"Scapegoating Muslims may be a Texas Republican strategist’s idea of ‘solid gold’ to whip up their voters, but Democrats have no intention of indulging this political creepshow, particularly after the recent violence targeting places of faith," they said. "Our focus is the costs families face thanks to rampant, non-stop Trump corruption."

MICHIGAN SENATE RACE: EL-SAYED’S TIES TO EXTREMIST FUEL ANTISEMITISM CONCERNS AMONG JEWISH VOTERS

The Connecticut Democrat added that he planned to meet with members of the Muslim community who shared concerns about the Muslim Brotherhood, "which appears to be a terrorist organization," while advocating for "tolerance and inclusion."

The offices of Whitehouse and Welch referred Fox News Digital to the joint statement when asked why the senators chose to boycott rather than attend and challenge the witnesses directly. The offices of Hirono and Padilla had not responded by publication time.

Cruz and the hearing’s witnesses rejected the Democrats’ characterization of the proceeding as an attack on Muslims generally.

Lara Burns, a retired FBI special agent who helped lead a terrorism-financing investigation into what was once the largest Muslim charity in the United States, the Holy Land Foundation, warned that Americans should not disregard evidence because it is politically controversial.

"For decades, narratives have been intentionally seeded into public discourse that portray terrorist organizations as resistance movements," Burns testified before arguing Americans cannot "ignore evidence introduced in federal court simply because that evidence is politically uncomfortable."

"The history of this network is not in question," she added. "It was made public decades ago, but few paid attention. Now is the time to pay attention and understand the facts."

item.title: The Left wants Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham to shut up and dribble when it comes to trans sports
item.description: Liberal sports media now wants Caitlin Clark to shut up and dribble on transgender athletes after demanding she speak on cultural issues for years.
item.content:encoded:
All of a sudden, it is liberal members of the sports media who want athletes like Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham to stick to sports.

"Caitlin Clark just wants to shut up and dribble, and it's time we respect that," far-left sportswriter Dan Wolken wrote in a Yahoo column this week.

The column is in reference to Clark declining to comment on Cunningham's recent remarks about wanting to keep biological males out of female athletics.

"I think for us, it's not really a discussion we have in our locker room," Clark said when asked about Cunningham's comments. "I think that's for leagues and governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions, but our focus is on basketball. That's what we talk about and how we can get wins, and obviously we didn't do that tonight."

On the surface, we agree with the left's newfound stance on Caitlin Clark.

Clark does not owe anyone a comment on transgender participation in sports or any other issue unrelated to basketball. She has spent her entire life preparing to become a professional basketball player. She has no obligation to become the public face of any cultural issue.

The problem is that many of the very people suddenly insisting Clark should be left alone spent the past three seasons refusing to leave her alone.

ELLE DUNCAN BLAMES CAITLIN CLARK, HER FANS FOR MEDIA SMEAR CAMPAIGN WHILE IGNORING FACTS

The same commentators now criticizing conservatives for asking Clark about transgender athletes repeatedly demanded that she address what they described as the racism and homophobia directed at the WNBA's Black and lesbian players following her arrival in the league.

Just last week, former ESPN host Elle Duncan called for Clark to do exactly that.

"I would love for it to be very clear to the people who think they are her fans but are using her, if she would say, 'Stop that s---. I don't want it. I'm tired of it,'" Duncan said on The Sports Gossip Show podcast. "As opposed to what we've seen, which is, 'The media makes up these narratives. The media makes up this discourse.'"

Hill, David Dennis Jr., Cari Champion, Ros Gold-Onwude, Dan Le Batard and countless others made similar demands. They wanted Clark to legitimize their manufactured crisis.

Notice that Wolken never argued the media should respect Clark's then.

Now, they all want her to shut up and dribble.

DAN LE BATARD CLAIMS ESPN IS RUN BY MCAFEE AND 'WHITE PEOPLE' AFTER LAYOFFS, SLANDERS OUTKICK IN UNHINGED RANT

Next, let's try to have the type of conversation that few have managed to have about Caitlin Clark. A nuanced one.

The conservatives involved in this debate do not come away looking particularly strong either. It's fair to ask Clark about transgender athletes, given the attention the issue has received over the past week. However, calling her a "coward" for declining to answer reeks of the same entitlement conservatives often accuse the left of displaying.

"Caitlin Clark might be the biggest coward in the history of sports," Daily Wire commentator Matt Walsh said. "She refuses to say anything about the anti-white racism she has been subjected to since coming into the league. She punts on the trans question, which is the easiest question you could ever be asked. No spine."

Meanwhile, Awful Announcing is enjoying the spectacle, gloating that "Conservative media ate Caitlin Clark up. Now they're spitting her out."

We understand why some people believe Clark should simply say that biological males should not compete in women's sports. For one, that position is hardly fringe. According to Pew Research, roughly 78% of Americans agree. That includes Democrats, Republicans, and independents.

The WNBA exists because sports are separated by sex. There would be no WNBA if men's and women's athletics were not separate. Howard Bryant's comparison this week between Cunningham's comments and Colin Kaepernick's protests was both ignorant and desperate.

Still, the topic of transgender athletes has become deeply divisive in American politics. Therefore, it is entirely understandable that Clark would rather stay out of it entirely.

Cunningham is not a villain for sharing that view. Clark is also not a coward for declining to discuss it. Both statements can be true at once.

As has so often been the case throughout her WNBA career, Caitlin Clark once again looks like the only adult in the room.

While everyone around her manufactures outrage, she continues to handle herself like a professional.

Amid the toxic discourse, Clark has put together one of the greatest seven-game stretches in WNBA history, averaging 26.1 points and 8.6 assists per game.

Caitlin Clark is one of the few star athletes in America today who just wants to play ball. No amount of political pressure will change that.

As hard as it is for some to fathom, Caitlin Clark isn't interested in the culture war. She just wants to play basketball.

Let her.

item.title: Miranda Kerr's ultra-specific diet includes venison for breakfast, no eggs or seed oils
item.description: Miranda Kerr revealed her strict diet, including venison for breakfast, no eggs and zero seed oils or dairy. She said eating better has helped her feel better.
item.content:encoded:
Miranda Kerr recently detailed her ultra healthy, if a bit unique, diet, which includes eating venison for breakfast and cutting out eggs altogether.

"I love food, but when I got sick, I had to learn even more that food is medicine," the former Victoria’s Secret Angel told Kristin Cavallari on her "Let’s be Honest" podcast. "So, I love to have nutritious and delicious foods that feed my soul, but, at the same time, I don’t crave like unhealthy food anymore because I know how detrimental that can be to my body on the inside, not even about what it looks like on the outside, but on the inside.

"I want to have vitality and energy and that’s kind of why I eat healthy."

Two years ago, Kerr revealed she was diagnosed with proctitis, a form of irritable bowl syndrome, when she was pregnant with her second son six years earlier.

MIRANDA KERR RECALLS FIRST MEETING EX ORLANDO BLOOM'S FIANCEE KATY PERRY: 'WE JUST IMMEDIATELY GOT ALONG'

She told Get the Gloss at the time she drank a liter of celery juice a day, which is known to be an anti-inflammatory, and said she is now in remission.

The 43-year-old supermodel told Cavallari she wants to be able to run around with her grandkids someday, "be baking them cakes like my grandma did for me" and feel healthy "for as long as" she can.

"‘Cause I think that’s more important than what you look like," she argued. "It’s so much more important that you feel that vitality, and that’s why I say that my non-negotiables are meditation. Like, I’m doing that instead of working out, I guess you could say, with the busy life that I have right now, but that’s the choice that I make because that’s what feeds me."

She said other people might be "really fed" by going for a run in the morning, for example. 

"Each to their own. You have to find what elevates you, what de-stresses you," she said. 

She also loves dance parties with her kids.

Kerr shares Flynn, 15, with ex-husband Orlando Bloom and Hart, 8, Myles, 6, and Pierre, 2, with her husband, Snapchat founder Evan Spiegel.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

She said she’s been drinking Noni juice, which she calls a "superfood superfruit," in the morning for 30 years since she was 13.

"What I love about it is it’s full of antioxidants, and it has a lot of vitamins and minerals."

She said she drinks a 30-millimeter shot, and her youngest child has some as well, but she admitted her teenager is "not into it."

Kerr then has a marshmallow tea "because that’s good for the gut lining. S,o I get the marshmallow leaf, and then I put it and brew it in hot water."

That's followed by a few tablespoons of coconut yogurt with honey and a bite of a banana.

"I do all of this before I have my coffee. I get to my coffee, and my coffee is my moment where I’m in bliss," she admitted.

Her Fabula brand coffee, which she said is mold- and lead-free, includes coconut milk from high-end grocery store Erewhon and maple syrup.

She also doesn’t eat eggs.

"I do proteins, like meats like venison, bison, lamb, turkey. I eat all the meats that aren’t mass-produced for the reasons that we all know," she explained. 

MIRANDA KERR'S HUSBAND, EVAN SPIEGEL, PRAISES HER 'VERY DIFFERENT' CO-PARENTING RELATIONSHIP WITH ORLANDO BLOOM

"I’m not much of a fruit girl, to be honest, but I will have a banana, and I also think a banana is a great snack to go," she said. "I do love mangoes."

She also stays away from dairy and wheat, "and I’m very specific about the oils, so only cooking with coconut oil or avocado oil. No seed oils."

Kerr said she does tallow sometimes, "mostly for the kids." She also tries to get them to eat sourdough because they refuse to eat gluten-free bread.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Lots of squash, carrots and parsnips are also on the menu. 

"And I do have a little bit of salmon but not too much because of the mercury that’s in salmon," she said.

The model said she used to "live on sushi" when she lived in New York, but she doesn't eat it anymore because of the possibility of parasites.

"I do love caviar," she admitted. "Caviar’s good. There’s no parasites there."

As far as sweets, she likes carob, and she and her younger kids have tea parties where they drink lemon balm tea with carob.

"I do like chocolate, and, so, I also will make, like, a carob hot chocolate with coconut milk, maple syrup, carob. It’s really good," she added.

item.title: Search for Amelia Earhart's long-lost plane reignites with ambitious new expedition
item.description: The Taraia Object Expedition departs on Oct. 7 for Nikumaroro Island to investigate a satellite-imaged anomaly believed to be Amelia Earhart's long-missing plane.
item.content:encoded:
Researchers are gearing up to resume their search for Amelia Earhart's lost plane in the Pacific Ocean after setbacks delayed the search.

Purdue University officials said in a recent statement that researchers will travel to Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific to investigate the Taraia Object, a satellite-imaged anomaly believed by some to be Earhart's lost Lockheed Electra.

The expedition, called the Taraia Object Expedition, will depart on Oct. 7.

AMELIA EARHART MYSTERY EXPEDITION HALTED AS RESEARCHERS SEEK ANSWERS ON MISSING PLANE

"The expedition seeks to help complete the historic journey that ended with her disappearance 89 years ago," officials said. 

If researchers confirm the Taraia Object is Earhart's airplane, they hope to conduct a full-scale archaeological excavation next year with the proper permissions, Purdue spokesperson Trevor Peters told Fox News Digital.

"The eventual curation of the wreckage has been the subject of discussions with [the Republic of] Kiribati, and although nothing has been finalized, ALI [the Archaeological Legacy Institute] and the Purdue Research Foundation share a dream of returning the plane to Purdue to be displayed, consistent with Amelia's original wishes," he added.

The expedition is based on researchers' belief that Earhart's plane came down near Nikumaroro, known as the Nikumaroro Hypothesis.

NEWLY RELEASED AMELIA EARHART DOCUMENTS REVEAL VIVID DETAILS OF JAPAN'S ROLE IN SEARCH FOR DOOMED AVIATOR

Supporters of the theory believe that Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan became stranded on the remote island after failing to reach Howland Island — possibly dying as castaways.

Earhart disappeared on July 2, 1937, while attempting to become the first female pilot to fly around the world.

She and Noonan lost contact during one of the final legs of their journey, going missing after leaving Lae, New Guinea, en route to Howland Island.

She was 39 years old at the time and one of the most famous people in the world.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The upcoming expedition was announced last year but was delayed while officials awaited approval from the government of Kiribati. The country's cabinet has since approved the mission.

Richard Pettigrew, founder and executive director of the Archaeological Legacy Institute, which is leading the expedition, said that he is "grateful for the patience and enthusiasm of everyone who has followed this journey with us."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"The evidence supporting the Nikumaroro Hypothesis remains compelling, and the only way to answer this question is to go to Nikumaroro, inspect the Taraia Object firsthand and follow the evidence wherever it leads," Pettigrew said in a statement.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The story of Earhart's disappearance has captivated Americans for decades and has been the subject of ongoing research.

Last year, the National Archives released over 4,600 pages of previously unsealed government records related to Earhart's 1937 disappearance, including her final known radio transmissions.

More recently, pilot Justin Myers said he identified a possible image of Earhart's missing Lockheed Electra in Google Earth imagery of Nikumaroro.

item.title: Spokane fire survivor finds 'joy' through Jesus after alleged arson destroys home and belongings
item.description: Christopher Guyton says losing his home in the Spokane wildfire strengthened his Christian faith and inspired him to spread the Gospel to others.
item.content:encoded:
Spokane wildfire survivor Christopher Guyton said losing his home to one of Washington state’s most devastating wildfires strengthened his faith and inspired him to spread the Gospel.

Guyton shared his faithful message Wednesday on "America Reports" as fire survivors across the Spokane area look to rebuild their lives after three separate fires reportedly burned over 10,000 acres and destroyed more than 700 structures.

"I'm able to see very clearly the love of Jesus Christ," Guyton said. "There are a lot of people out there that lost their homes that don't have Jesus, and that is way worse... what this makes me want to do is go spread the Gospel."

SPENCER PRATT REACTS TO SPOKANE DEVASTATION WITH BLUNT WILDFIRE WARNING AND MESSAGE OF FAITH

Flames tore through the Spokane area over the weekend, leaving neighborhoods with charred vehicles, melted plastic recycling bins and ash-covered lots that were once homes.

Guyton, an audio designer who moved to Spokane in 2020, lamented how his family and so many others lost "everything" in the "blink of an eye."

The Spokane resident lost cherished personal belongings, including his music studio and retro video game collection, though his wife, two children and cat escaped unharmed.

"My 3-year-old, she doesn't really understand why we can't go home," he told Fox News. "My 1-year-old is a little bit too young to really understand anything.

"We haven't showed them any of this just because we feel like it would just be too traumatic for them."

Guyton expressed gratitude for the support of his church community as he and his family look to rebuild their lives.

"It's been pretty difficult, but, luckily, we have a really supportive church family, and we are just super blessed with everything that we've been given to just try to start putting the pieces back together," Guyton said.

He said navigating the loss of a home has been easier because of his faith, explaining that the "joy" he finds in Christianity helps ease the pain.

VIRGIN MARY STATUE BECOMES BEACON OF HOPE AFTER CALIFORNIA WILDFIRES, FOX NATION EXPLORES

"[My pastor] always talks about the difference between joy and happiness," Guyton said. "He says, ‘Joy is something that you get from God, and when you have joy, you can still feel sadness, but there's a lightness to that sadness.’"

The grief that comes with such a devastating loss, Guyton said, feels more manageable because of his relationship with God, adding that he hopes to use his devastation to introduce more people to Jesus’ love.

"When you're depressed, sadness is really heavy, and happiness is really, really heavy as well. But we have joy because we have Jesus," Guyton said.

Aaron Farinacci, 37, was charged with first-degree arson after being accused of intentionally setting the Old Trails Fire, the largest of the three Spokane blazes. Officials say Farinacci was questioned by police about two other wildfires in 2025.

Guyton said Farinacci’s alleged arson is a "real shame" and only makes the tragedy "worse" as the family of four grapples with how to move forward without their home.

"I hope that all the authorities that are involved in this can find some way to make this right with everyone," he concluded.

item.title: Brewery behind Trump, McConnell death promotions now unveils 'Antifa Octoberfist' beer
item.description: Minocqua Brewing Company released its "Antifa Octoberfist" beer after Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Democratic primary for a Senate nomination.
item.content:encoded:
The Wisconsin brewery that previously drew national attention for promising free beer "the day" President Donald Trump dies and later announcing plans for a "half-price beer day" when Sen. "Now that another card-carrying member of ANTIFA has won the Democratic Primary in Michigan, we thought today would be a good day to announce that our seasonal Octoberfest is BACK--and it's call ‘Antifa Octoberfist!’" the post read.

On Tuesday, Abdul El-Sayed defeated Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., winning the Democratic nomination for Senate.

The brewery then shared the message printed on the back of the cans about punching Nazis.

"During World War II, America rose up against Nazi Germany and rejected the idea of fascism, which is defined as government lead by a strong man that fetishizes power, uses violence to quash opposition, demands absolute loyalty, and gains power by seducing those who perceive themselves as victims," the message reads.

WISCONSIN BREWERY THAT PROMISED FREE BEER WHEN TRUMP DIES NOW PLANS 'HALF-PRICE BEER DAY' WHEN MCCONNELL DIES

"Over the last 70 years, we’ve honored our American forefathers who vanquished fascism in Germany," it continued. "Of course it’s not OK to punch anyone, but it’s patriotic as hell to raise your fist against fascism, reject its four tenets, and embrace the true American ideals of democracy, freedom, justice, and equality of opportunity."

The brewery previously sparked outrage by promising free beer on "the day" Trump dies in January, and again following the April shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner. On Monday, it announced plans for a "half-price beer day" for when McConnell dies.

The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported on July 27 that Wisconsin's Department of Revenue sent a notice to liberal activist and brewery owner Kirk Bangstad announcing plans to revoke the brewery’s permit.

WORLD-FAMOUS CATHOLIC SHRINE TORCHED, 'DEVIL IN A SKIRT' SCRAWLED ON VIRGIN MARY STATUE

The revocation of the beer permit was set to go into effect on Tuesday, but a spokesperson for Wisconsin's Department of Revenue told Fox News Digital in a statement Monday that "Minocqua Brewing Company has filed an administrative appeal, and, therefore, the permit will not be revoked, pending the outcome of the administrative appeal."

item.title: Russia deploys North Korean missile unit to Ukraine; Moscow-Pyongyang axis deepens: report
item.description: A Ukrainian intelligence official says Russia is deploying a North Korean unit with up to 120 ballistic missiles in its war against Ukraine.
item.content:encoded:
Russia has begun deploying a North Korean missile unit equipped with up to 120 ballistic missiles and six launchers for use in its war against Ukraine, a Ukrainian intelligence official told told Reuters Wednesday.

The reported escalation marks a deepening military partnership between Moscow and Pyongyang, with around 90 North Korean personnel expected to be stationed in Russia's western Voronezh region to support the new unit, according to Andrii Cherniak of Ukraine's Main Directorate of Intelligence (HUR).

Cherniak also claimed Pyongyang has already delivered a fresh batch of 40 KN-23 and KN-24 ballistic missiles to Russian forces, Reuters said.

RUSSIA LAUNCHES BALLISTIC MISSILE ATTACK ON KYIV HOURS AFTER ZELENSKYY WARNS OF MAJOR STRIKE

Final details of the deployment are expected to be finalized during high-level talks next month.

The intelligence report follows a massive Russian barrage against Kyiv and the surrounding region Aug. 4. 

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Moscow launched 24 ballistic missiles, four cruise missiles and 115 drones overnight, killing at least 17 people.

Zelenskyy argued more lives could have been saved had Western allies replenished Ukraine's depleted stockpiles of air defense interceptors.

Zelenskyy previously warned that Moscow had been preparing since June to receive additional North Korean military personnel in the Voronezh region, according to reports.

RUSSIA UNLEASHES NEARLY 600 MISSILES AND DRONES ON KYIV IN DEADLIEST STRIKE SINCE MAY

Cherniak told Reuters a Russian strike in late July marked the first recorded use of North Korean ballistic missiles against Ukrainian targets since August 2025.

According to HUR estimates, Russia has received approximately 150 KN-23 and KN-24 missiles from North Korea since late 2023.

Military analysts say Russia is increasingly relying on ballistic weapons because they require advanced defense systems — such as the U.S.-made Patriot — to intercept.

The Washington-based Institute for the Study of War (ISW) assessed that Russia is deliberately incorporating more ballistic missiles into its long-range strike packages to maximize pressure on Ukraine's limited air defenses.

ISW added that North Korea is gaining critical battlefield data from the conflict, allowing Pyongyang to refine its missile performance using Russian operational experience.

ALARMING MISSILE REPORT DRAWS FORCEFUL RESPONSE FROM TRUMP AS IRAN WAR TESTS AMERICA’S ARSENAL

North Korea has emerged as one of Moscow's key military allies since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began.

Reuters reported that Pyongyang has supplied millions of artillery shells and previously sent 14,000 troops to Russia's Kursk region to counter Ukraine's 2024 cross-border incursion.

Cherniak also noted that roughly 9,500 North Korean troops are still in Kursk, though they are not engaged in active combat right now.

A report by the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD) states that, since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, North Korea has supplied Moscow with large quantities of artillery and rocket ammunition, cannon and rocket artillery systems and ballistic missiles.

The policy institute described the Russia-North Korea relationship as one of the "most consequential among the Axis" and the only partnership in which one member has deployed troops in combat to assist another.
